frameworks.name: 10-Stage Revenue Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A progression from zero to $100M+ revenue with eight business functions tracked across each stage; each stage has distinct constraints and required changes to graduate.

claims.text: Exceptional individuals demonstrate depth across multiple unrelated domains simultaneously. Alex Hormozi cites Joe Rogan as an example: deep in MMA, comedy, biohacking, space exploration, and politics—each pursued independently rather than following a template. This combination of depth across incongruent domains signals high personal agency.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Most people adopt pre-packaged identity templates—personality off-the-shelf (flannels, trucker hat, beer preference, political alignment as a bundle). These are pattern-matched instantly by observers, signaling low distinctiveness and low agency because the holder did not think independently about each belief.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: When an individual's stated positions violate predicted patterns (e.g., a conservative-coded person expressing pro-LGBTQ+ values, or demonstrating philosophical depth unexpectedly), an observer's brain cannot pattern-match and must update its internal schema; this attention-forcing mechanism is what makes a person appear 'exceptional' or possess 'x-factor.'
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: When expectations are violated, the observer must update their schema, forcing cognitive attention and creating perceived distinctiveness; distinctiveness requires the target individual to have thought independently rather than adopted pre-packaged beliefs.

claims.text: Entrepreneurs who think for themselves end up unique because they do not follow belief-bundles tied to ideological or cultural templates; they pick and choose across domains, which is the marker of independent thought and high agency.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: does not imply that following a template results in incompetence; only that it results in low distinctiveness

claims.text: There is a 10-stage revenue roadmap from zero to $100M+ that most companies (fewer than 1%) complete. Each stage requires specific changes across eight business functions: the constraints at each stage are distinct, each has observable symptoms, and the steps to graduate from one stage to the next are systematic.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: applies across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar

numbers.axis: percentage of companies that complete the full 0-to-$100M+ roadmap

practices.text: Go to acquisition.com/roadmap to download the 10-stage revenue roadmap from zero to $100M+, which includes constraints, symptoms, and graduation steps for eight business functions.
